prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 7 "Service technician hours": indemnified in all 3 earlier cases; when indemnified t per hr about 84 (80% range 56 to 106); revealed per hr: 44-49 (case 21), >=81 (case 39), >=81 (case 39), so this line (6.75 hr) about 566 (381 to 715)
- line 8 "Helper hours": no earlier line of this grade; level of the other hourly grades; when indemnified t per hr about 68 (80% range 27 to 173), so this line (5.75 hr) about 394 (156 to 992)
- line 9 "Rock wool pipe insulation": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 24 (80% range 17.9 to 37); revealed per pc: >=22 (case 39), so this line (6 pc) about 146 (107 to 222)
- line 12 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 13 of 28 earlier cases, t = 0 in 15; when indemnified t per pc about 80 (80% range 72 to 88); revealed per pc: >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27), >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34), >=65 (case 39)
- line 13 "Construction waste disposal": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 62 (80% range 45 to 94); revealed per pc: >=57 (case 18)
- line 17 "Processing flat fee": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 6 earlier cases; no price evidence

items.rationale: The indoor heating-pipe repair is covered under §2.4.3(a), and §7.1.7(c) covers matching fittings. Four elbows at about €11 each give €44 gross.

Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) allow these fittings if the reconnection used existing 28 mm pipework; the listed 15 mm replacement tube does not establish that. If verified, five elbows at about €20 each give €100 gross.
Under §§7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e), this elbow is payable only if it matches a documented connection in the repaired run. If verified, a single elbow is estimated at €21 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) allows minor fixings used in the pipe repair without requiring each one to be matched individually. Eight screws at about €1.25 each give €10 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary supports fitted to the repaired run, provided the clamp size suits the installation. Four clamps at about €4.50 each give €18 gross.
Sections 2.4.3(a) and 7.1.7(c) cover like-for-like copper tube used to renew the failed run. If the full 6.4 m was needed for the documented repair, about €12 per metre gives €77 gross.

Section 7.1.7(g) covers customary labour for the pipe repair, but §7.1.5 excludes time spent on unrelated jobs. The full 6.75-hour benchmark is €566 gross if those hours are attributable to the repair.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary helper time on the repair, not general maintenance or flooring work. The full 5.75-hour benchmark is €394 gross if the hours are substantiated as repair labour.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow reinstatement of the pre-loss insulation on the repaired pipe. The gross benchmark for all six pieces is €146.

Section 7.1.7(c) covers wire used to secure the reinstated insulation, but §7.1.8(e) excludes any quantity not attributable to the job. If the full 2 kg is substantiated, about €8 per kg gives €16 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) expressly allows lump-sum minor repair consumables, while §7.1.8(c) bars duplication of separately billed parts. A modest nonduplicative allowance is €20 gross.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge per contractor per invoice. This is the only travel line, so the gross benchmark is €80.

Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover disposal of repair debris, not waste from the undamaged storage-room floor. The generic line is payable only to the extent the pipe-repair waste can be identified; the benchmark for one eligible disposal charge is €62 gross.
Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude work in the unaffected hallway; §7.1.6 does not extend cover to a separate surface. If the work were eligible, 12 m² at about €13 per m² would be €156 gross.
Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude replacement of the expressly undamaged floor in the separate storage room. If eligible, ordinary removal and replacement of 15 m² at €50 per m² would be €750 gross.
Section 7.1.8(a) excludes routine servicing unrelated to the basement leak. If eligible, a simple service performed while already on site would be about €75 gross.

Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes processing charges billed in addition to itemised labour and materials. The conditional €15 gross estimate is nominal, as the references provide no payable price evidence.
